newsitem.title: FRANCE: Union calls for talks over Elf strike.
newsitem.headline: Union calls for talks over Elf strike.

text.p: Striking French refinery workers called for urgent meetings with Elf Aquitaine bosses on Monday to discuss their demands in a five-day stoppage over job cuts.
An Elf refinery official said the company had offered talks from Wednesday to resolve a strike that has left all three of its main French refineries idle since at least last Thursday.
But one of the unions leading the protests, the CFTC, said there was no sign of the strike cracking and urged Elf's Antar refining subsidiary to come to the table sooner.

"In the company's own interests, the management of Elf Antar France must open negotiations urgently, bearing in mind the fierce determination of staff to get concrete and tangible results," the union said in a statement.
A spokesman for the CFDT, France's biggest union, also called for immediate negotiations.
Elf had no immediate comment on the timing of talks.
The strike was originally called as a 24-hour protest against plans to cut 330 jobs, or 10 percent of the Elf Antar workforce, over 18 months.
The CFTC said on Monday, however, this was one of four areas it wanted to negotiate. Others were improved conditions for workers on evening shifts, salaries and shorter working hours.
At the same time unions said they were testing support for wider disruption at other French refineries, in a move seen as an attempt to build on last month's 12-day truckers' strike.
Elf Antar staff were due to decide on Monday afternoon whether to prolong their own strike further. They have so far pledged to stay on strike until Tuesday morning.
The Elf strike affects all three refineries which France's largest oil company owns and operates inside the country.
These in turn represent 76 percent of Elf's share of refining capacity in Europe, according to its annual report.

The 95,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) Grandpuits refinery near Paris was the first plant to close last Wednesday. The 211,000 bpd Donges plant in western France and the 120,000 bpd Feyzin refinery near Lyon have been idle since last Thursday.

Besides its three self-operated plants, Elf has a 10-percent stake in the small Reichstett refinery in Strasbourg, eastern France, and is the 70-percent majority shareholder in Britain's Milford Haven plant.
In Germany, Elf owns the Brunsbuttel asphalt plant and has an 8.33 percent in the Schwedt oil refinery.
